#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Dashboard server with SAFE_MODE validation.

Validates that HTML files contain only approved CSS classes before serving.
"""

import http.server
import socketserver
import os
import re
import sys
from html.parser import HTMLParser

# Safety configuration
SAFE_MODE = True
PORT = 8000
DASHBOARD_DIR = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))

# Approved CSS classes - only these are allowed in served HTML files
APPROVED_CSS_CLASSES = {
    # Layout
    "container",
    "row",
    "col",
    "header",
    "footer",
    "sidebar",
    "main",
    "content",
    "wrapper",
    "section",
    # Dashboard components
    "dashboard",
    "dashboard-title",
    "dashboard-header",
    "dashboard-body",
    "dashboard-grid",
    "card",
    "card-title",
    "card-body",
    "card-header",
    "card-footer",
    "metric",
    "metric-label",
    "metric-value",
    "chart",
    "chart-container",
    "table",
    "table-row",
    "table-cell",
    "table-header",
    # Status / utility
    "status",
    "status-ok",
    "status-warning",
    "status-error",
    "badge",
    "btn",
    "btn-primary",
    "btn-secondary",
    "hidden",
    "visible",
    "active",
    "inactive",
    # Typography
    "title",
    "subtitle",
    "text",
    "text-muted",
    "text-bold",
}


class CSSClassExtractor(HTMLParser):
    """Extracts all CSS class names used in an HTML document."""

    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        self.classes_found = set()

    def handle_starttag(self, tag, attrs):
        for name, value in attrs:
            if name == "class" and value:
                for cls in value.split():
                    cls = cls.strip()
                    if cls:
                        self.classes_found.add(cls)


def extract_css_classes(html_content: str) -> set:
    """Return the set of CSS class names referenced in the HTML."""
    parser = CSSClassExtractor()
    try:
        parser.feed(html_content)
    except Exception as exc:
        # On parse error, fail closed (treat as if everything is unapproved)
        print(f"[SAFE_MODE] HTML parse error: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
        return {"<parse-error>"}
    return parser.classes_found


def validate_html_classes(html_content: str):
    """
    Validate that an HTML document only uses approved CSS classes.

    Returns (is_valid: bool, disallowed: set[str]).
    """
    used = extract_css_classes(html_content)
    disallowed = used - APPROVED_CSS_CLASSES
    return (len(disallowed) == 0, disallowed)


class SafeDashboardHandler(http.server.SimpleHTTPRequestHandler):
    """HTTP handler that validates HTML against the approved CSS class list."""

    def do_GET(self):
        # Resolve the requested filesystem path safely within DASHBOARD_DIR
        requested = self.path.split("?", 1)[0].split("#", 1)[0]
        rel_path = requested.lstrip("/")
        if rel_path == "":
            rel_path = "index.html"

        fs_path = os.path.normpath(os.path.join(DASHBOARD_DIR, rel_path))
        if not fs_path.startswith(DASHBOARD_DIR):
            self.send_error(403, "Forbidden: path traversal blocked")
            return

        # Only validate HTML files; pass other assets through to the default handler.
        if fs_path.lower().endswith((".html", ".htm")) and os.path.isfile(fs_path):
            if SAFE_MODE:
                try:
                    with open(fs_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                        html_content = f.read()
                except OSError as exc:
                    self.send_error(500, f"Could not read file: {exc}")
                    return

                is_valid, disallowed = validate_html_classes(html_content)
                if not is_valid:
                    msg = (
                        "Refusing to serve {path}: contains unapproved CSS "
                        "classes: {bad}".format(
                            path=rel_path, bad=sorted(disallowed)
                        )
                    )
                    print(f"[SAFE_MODE] {msg}", file=sys.stderr)
                    self.send_error(403, msg)
                    return

                # Validation passed — serve the (already-read) content directly.
                encoded = html_content.encode("utf-8")
                self.send_response(200)
                self.send_header("Content-Type", "text/html; charset=utf-8")
                self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(encoded)))
                self.send_header("X-Safe-Mode", "true")
                self.end_headers()
                self.wfile.write(encoded)
                return

        # Fall back to the default static-file behavior for non-HTML requests.
        super().do_GET()

    def translate_path(self, path):
        # Ensure the default handler also serves out of DASHBOARD_DIR.
        original_cwd = os.getcwd()
        try:
            os.chdir(DASHBOARD_DIR)
            return super().translate_path(path)
        finally:
            os.chdir(original_cwd)


def main():
    print(f"[serve_dashboard] SAFE_MODE = {SAFE_MODE}")
    print(f"[serve_dashboard] Approved classes: {len(APPROVED_CSS_CLASSES)}")
    print(f"[serve_dashboard] Serving {DASHBOARD_DIR} on http://localhost:{PORT}")

    os.chdir(DASHBOARD_DIR)
    with socketserver.TCPServer(("", PORT), SafeDashboardHandler) as httpd:
        try:
            httpd.serve_forever()
        except KeyboardInterrupt:
            print("\n[serve_dashboard] Shutting down.")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Dashboard server with SAFE_MODE validation.

Serves files on localhost:6060 only when SAFE_MODE validation passes:
HTML files are scanned and only allowed to be served if every CSS class
they reference appears in APPROVED_CSS_CLASSES.
"""

import http.server
import socketserver
import os
import sys
from html.parser import HTMLParser

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Safety configuration
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

SAFE_MODE = True
HOST = "localhost"
PORT = 6060
DASHBOARD_DIR = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))

# Approved CSS classes - only these are allowed in served HTML files.
APPROVED_CSS_CLASSES = {
    # Layout
    "container", "row", "col",
    "header", "footer", "sidebar", "main", "content", "wrapper", "section",
    # Dashboard components
    "dashboard", "dashboard-title", "dashboard-header",
    "dashboard-body", "dashboard-grid",
    "card", "card-title", "card-body", "card-header", "card-footer",
    "metric", "metric-label", "metric-value",
    "chart", "chart-container",
    "table", "table-row", "table-cell", "table-header",
    # Status / utility
    "status", "status-ok", "status-warning", "status-error",
    "badge", "btn", "btn-primary", "btn-secondary",
    "hidden", "visible", "active", "inactive",
    # Typography
    "title", "subtitle", "text", "text-muted", "text-bold",
}


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Validation
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

class CSSClassExtractor(HTMLParser):
    """Extracts all CSS class names used in an HTML document."""

    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        self.classes_found = set()
        self.parse_error = False

    def handle_starttag(self, tag, attrs):
        for name, value in attrs:
            if name == "class" and value:
                for cls in value.split():
                    cls = cls.strip()
                    if cls:
                        self.classes_found.add(cls)

    def error(self, message):  # pragma: no cover (Python <3.10 compat)
        self.parse_error = True


def extract_css_classes(html_content: str):
    """Return (classes_used: set[str], parse_ok: bool)."""
    parser = CSSClassExtractor()
    try:
        parser.feed(html_content)
        parser.close()
    except Exception as exc:
        print(f"[SAFE_MODE] HTML parse error: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
        return parser.classes_found, False
    return parser.classes_found, not parser.parse_error


def validate_html_classes(html_content: str):
    """
    Validate that an HTML document only uses approved CSS classes.

    Returns (is_valid: bool, disallowed: set[str], parse_ok: bool).
    """
    used, parse_ok = extract_css_classes(html_content)
    if not parse_ok:
        # Fail closed on parse errors.
        return False, set(), False
    disallowed = used - APPROVED_CSS_CLASSES
    return (len(disallowed) == 0), disallowed, True


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Request handler
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

class SafeDashboardHandler(http.server.SimpleHTTPRequestHandler):
    """HTTP handler that validates HTML against the approved CSS class list."""

    server_version = "SafeDashboard/1.0"

    def _resolve_path(self, url_path: str):
        """Map a URL path to a filesystem path inside DASHBOARD_DIR."""
        requested = url_path.split("?", 1)[0].split("#", 1)[0]
        rel_path = requested.lstrip("/")
        if rel_path == "" or rel_path.endswith("/"):
            rel_path = os.path.join(rel_path, "index.html")

        fs_path = os.path.normpath(os.path.join(DASHBOARD_DIR, rel_path))
        # Block path traversal outside DASHBOARD_DIR.
        if not (fs_path == DASHBOARD_DIR or fs_path.startswith(DASHBOARD_DIR + os.sep)):
            return None
        return fs_path

    def do_GET(self):
        if not SAFE_MODE:
            self.send_error(503, "Server unavailable: SAFE_MODE is disabled")
            return

        fs_path = self._resolve_path(self.path)
        if fs_path is None:
            self.send_error(403, "Forbidden: path traversal blocked")
            return

        if not os.path.exists(fs_path):
            self.send_error(404, "Not found")
            return

        # Directories: try index.html inside.
        if os.path.isdir(fs_path):
            fs_path = os.path.join(fs_path, "index.html")
            if not os.path.isfile(fs_path):
                self.send_error(404, "Not found")
                return

        if fs_path.lower().endswith((".html", ".htm")):
            self._serve_validated_html(fs_path)
            return

        # Non-HTML assets: delegate to default static handler.
        super().do_GET()

    def _serve_validated_html(self, fs_path: str):
        try:
            with open(fs_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                html_content = f.read()
        except OSError as exc:
            self.send_error(500, f"Could not read file: {exc}")
            return

        is_valid, disallowed, parse_ok = validate_html_classes(html_content)

        if not parse_ok:
            msg = f"Refusing to serve {os.path.basename(fs_path)}: HTML failed to parse"
            print(f"[SAFE_MODE] {msg}", file=sys.stderr)
            self.send_error(403, msg)
            return

        if not is_valid:
            bad = sorted(disallowed)
            msg = (
                f"Refusing to serve {os.path.basename(fs_path)}: "
                f"unapproved CSS classes: {bad}"
            )
            print(f"[SAFE_MODE] {msg}", file=sys.stderr)
            self.send_error(403, msg)
            return

        encoded = html_content.encode("utf-8")
        self.send_response(200)
        self.send_header("Content-Type", "text/html; charset=utf-8")
        self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(encoded)))
        self.send_header("X-Safe-Mode", "true")
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(encoded)

    def translate_path(self, path):
        original_cwd = os.getcwd()
        try:
            os.chdir(DASHBOARD_DIR)
            return super().translate_path(path)
        finally:
            os.chdir(original_cwd)

    def log_message(self, format, *args):
        sys.stderr.write(
            "[serve_dashboard] %s - %s\n" % (self.address_string(), format % args)
        )


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Entry point
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

class _ReusableTCPServer(socketserver.TCPServer):
    allow_reuse_address = True


def main():
    if not SAFE_MODE:
        print("[serve_dashboard] Refusing to start: SAFE_MODE is disabled.",
              file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)

    print(f"[serve_dashboard] SAFE_MODE      = {SAFE_MODE}")
    print(f"[serve_dashboard] Approved class count = {len(APPROVED_CSS_CLASSES)}")
    print(f"[serve_dashboard] Dashboard dir  = {DASHBOARD_DIR}")
    print(f"[serve_dashboard] Listening on   http://{HOST}:{PORT}")

    os.chdir(DASHBOARD_DIR)
    with _ReusableTCPServer((HOST, PORT), SafeDashboardHandler) as httpd:
        try:
            httpd.serve_forever()
        except KeyboardInterrupt:
            print("\n[serve_dashboard] Shutting down.")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
